title: 2.1.7 Add an else
description: Extend an if statement with an else branch to handle both outcomes. Auto-graded.
sourceRef: designed: practice for 'The else Clause', book 2.1.3

steps.title: Keep your if statement
steps.instructions: Start with a variable called score holding a number and an if statement that checks score >= 70.

steps.title: Add an else branch
steps.instructions: Directly after the closing brace of the if block, add an else block. Inside the else block, use console.log to print a message saying the score does not pass.

requirements.title: if block checks score >= 70 and logs
requirements.description: if statement's condition compares score to 70 with >=, and logs inside the block. Help: 2.1.3 (If / Else if / Else)

requirements.title: else branch logs
requirements.description: Code contains an else branch that calls console.log. Help: 2.1.3 (If / Else if / Else)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote JavaScript for the lab "2.1.7 Add an else". The task they were given: Start with a variable called score holding a number and an if statement that checks score >= 70. You cannot run their code: read it and judge what it WOULD do. Judge each criterion by whether the idea is achieved, however the student wrote it. Different variable and function names, template strings, arrow functions, semicolons, spacing, quotes and order are all fine. Do not require any particular structure unless the criterion names one. Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment never runs. Write each note for THIS student's own code: in a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise.
